links.outcome: Self-reported confidence versus accuracy on image-based rheumatology questions
links.effect: Confidence stayed high (7-10 for MCQs, 8-10 for image questions) although image accuracy ranged from 16% (Claude) to 56% (Gemini) and hallucinations occurred in 40% (Gemini) to 84% (Claude) of image responses.
links.quote: High confidence in incorrect image responses and frequent hallucinations highlight the need for caution when integrating these tools into clinical education or decision-making.

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks several commercial LLM and multimodal models on text- and image-based rheumatology questions without testing a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
